about: The intro's narration (cinema.gd): one clip for the Region, one for the Plot, one for the winery and the welcome. Spoken by the narrator voice (tools/voice/narrate.py renders each clip to game/assets3d/audio/voice/<clip>.mp3) and shown as captions. Facts from docs/science/regions-and-plots.md (Region summaries, Plot table) and docs/science/law.md; numbers are written out for the voice. The estate name and the year are shown as titles, never spoken (the clips are recorded once).

mosel.title: Mosel
mosel.sub: Germany · the world's largest steep-slope wine region
mosel.text: This is the Mosel, the largest steep-slope wine region in the world. Here the river has cut deep into the slate hills, and the vines climb almost straight up from the water. It is a cool place to grow grapes. The dark Devonian slate warms quickly in the sun, and the long, slow autumn keeps the acidity bright. Riesling from these slopes is light on its feet, precise, and moderate in alcohol.

cote-dor.title: Côte d'Or
cote-dor.sub: Burgundy, France · limestone and marl, facing the morning sun
cote-dor.text: This is the Côte d'Or, in Burgundy: a narrow escarpment facing east and south-east, where limestone and marl catch the morning sun. Here, more than anywhere, the exact patch of ground matters. The same Pinot Noir or Chardonnay can be a regional wine on the flat land below, a village wine, or a Premier Cru from the best part of the slope. Spring frost and summer heat test every grower.

napa.title: Napa Valley
napa.sub: California, USA · a Mediterranean climate cooled by the bay
napa.text: This is the Napa Valley, in California. A Mediterranean climate: rain in winter, long dry summers. In the south, fog and wind from San Pablo Bay keep Carneros cool. Up the valley it grows warmer, and the mountain vineyards sit above the summer fog. On the gravelly benches at the foot of the western hills, Cabernet Sauvignon finds its benchmark sites.

mosel-uferflur.text: Your land is Uferflur: one point six hectares of flat riverbank, just above the flood line. The soil is deep and fertile, and the vines grow with vigour. On still spring nights the cold air settles here, and in autumn the fog lies longest, so frost and rot need watching.

mosel-seitental.text: Your land is Seitental: a gentle side valley facing east, with loess over slate. The vines take the morning sun and stay cool in the afternoon, so they ripen late, and slowly.

mosel-blauschiefer.text: Your land is Blauschiefer-Hang: one point two hectares of blue Devonian slate, tilted at fifty-five per cent and facing south-west. The classic Middle Mosel Riesling slope. No tractor can work ground this steep. Most of the work here is done by hand.

mosel-terrassen.text: Your land is a set of slate terraces, held up by dry-stone walls and facing south. The steepest, warmest site on your stretch of the river, and the hardest to work: every task, from pruning to picking, is done by hand.

cotedor-plaine.text: Your land is Plaine des Bas: one hectare of flat land below the slope. Deep clay, fertile and easy to work, but prone to frost, and its wines can only be sold as Bourgogne.

cotedor-hautes.text: Your land is Plateau des Hautes, up on the Hautes-Côtes at around four hundred metres. Limestone, wind and cool nights: the grapes ripen late here, and in a hot year that slow ripening is a gift.

cotedor-village.text: Your land is Mi-Côte Villages: half a hectare of marl and limestone in the middle of the slope, facing east-south-east. Village wine, with the rules to match: dense planting, a limit on the buds you leave at pruning, and no irrigation.

cotedor-premiercru.text: Your land is Clos du Premier: half a hectare of thin limestone rubble facing the morning sun, in the sweet spot of the Côte. Premier Cru. The soil gives the vines little, and they give back concentration.

napa-floor.text: Your land is Valley Floor Loam: one hectare of heavy, fertile loam in the heart of the valley. The vines grow strongly, irrigation is allowed, and on cold spring nights the low spots can frost.

napa-carneros.text: Your land is Carneros Clay: one point two hectares of shallow clay over claypan, at the cool southern end of the valley, where fog and wind come in from the bay. Pinot Noir and Chardonnay are at home here. Cabernet Sauvignon struggles to ripen.

napa-mountain.text: Your land is a mountain hillside, high above the fog line. Thin volcanic and sedimentary soils, small crops, and wines with firm tannin.

napa-bench.text: Your land is Rutherford Bench: one hectare on the gravelly alluvial fan at the foot of the western hills. This is benchmark Cabernet Sauvignon country.

winery.text: And this is your winery. In the hall, the steel tanks wait for the harvest. Below, in the vaulted cellar, the wine will rest in wood.

welcome.text: The vines were planted three years ago, and this year they give their first real crop. What happens next is up to you: how you prune, when you pick, how you make the wine. Welcome to your estate.
